paragraphs.source_en: Others abandoned their nomad ways. The Ottoman Turks were originally pushed out of the steppes and into Anatolia in the thirteenth century by the Mongol expansion of Genghis Khan. Here they established themselves by adopting a European style of warfare relying on fortifications, and formed slave armies of captured Christian boys who were forced to convert to Islam, the famous Janissaries. 57 By the end of the thirteenth century the Ottomans had become a major threat to the states of Christendom, and in 1453 they captured Constantinople and brought to an end the Byzantine Empire. 58

paragraphs.source_en: Nomadic horsemen riding out of the steppes were the cause of two of the most defining moments of world history: the fall of the Western Roman Empire, and the conquest of Asia by the Mongols.
